fills.researcher_notes: No citable commissioning year found for this specific segment. Checked: sirteoil.com.ly (JS-rendered, no usable static content, no Wayback snapshots of content pages), noc.ly, Libya Herald/Observer archives, OPEC ASB (which lists the segment's length/diameter/capacity but not a start date), and a 2007 University of Salford PhD thesis on Libyan oil/gas development (Edwik, 'Oil Dependency, Economic Diversification and Development: A Case Study of Libya', recovered via Wayback since the live core.ac.uk copy 404s: https://web.archive.org/web/20210627234719/https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/40057706.pdf, verified OK/200 -- read only as a lead, gem.wiki-sourced). The thesis states 'Sirte Oil Company is now developing the Attahadi gas field in the Sirte basin ... The project calls for the installation of a 36inch gas line to carry the field's output to Marsa El Brega' in a section whose surrounding gas-reserves data and citations are dated to the early-to-mid 1990s (nearby table sourced to OPEC ASB 2005 for a 1990-2005 reserves series, with narrative discussion of a 1990-1991 reserve estimate revision). This suggests the Attahaddy field gas-gathering buildout (of which this km-91.5 segment is likely one leg) may be a 1990s-vintage development, not a 1960s-70s one -- notably later than most of the other Sirte-grid segments in this brief. However the thesis never states an exact commissioning year for this pipeline, and the diameter it names (36in) doesn't exactly match this sheet row's Diameter (30, 12) -- it may describe a related but different segment of the same Attahaddy gas-gathering system (this sheet's P1872 'Km-91.5-Brega' carries Diameter 36,16, a closer match). Not proposing a value given the ambiguity; flagged as a validity concern below instead.
